content: I want to build an app to save and manage bookmarks.

The baseline specification is drafted. No extension hooks are configured, so I'll stop here at the **spec review gate** — this is where SDD asks you to review before anything gets planned or built.

## 📄 Specification ready for your review

- **Feature directory**: `specs/001-bookmark-manager/`
- **Spec file**: `specs/001-bookmark-manager/spec.md`
- **Quality checklist**: passed on all items except the one open question below.

### What the spec proposes (in plain terms)

A personal, browser-based app to **save, find, and manage bookmarks**. It's sliced into independently valuable pieces:

| Priority | User story | What you get |
|----------|-----------|--------------|
| **P1** | Save a bookmark | Enter an address (title optional, auto-derived), it's validated and persisted |
| **P1** | Browse, search & open | See your list, search by keyword, open in a new tab |
| **P2** | Edit & delete | Fix titles/addresses, delete with a confirmation step |
| **P3** | Organize with tags | Label bookmarks and filter by tag |

P1 + P1 together are the minimum viable product; P2 and P3 layer on afterward.

It also covers edge cases (duplicate addresses, missing `https://`, empty state, long text) and sets measurable success criteria (e.g. find a bookmark among 100 in under 10 seconds, no data loss across restarts).

### One question before we plan

I made a reasonable v1 default but this is the biggest scope driver, so I'd like your call:

**Q1 — Who uses this app?**

| Option | Answer | Implications |
|--------|--------|--------------|
| **A** | Single user, no login (my default) | Simplest; one personal collection. No accounts/passwords in v1. |
| **B** | Multiple users, each with their own account & login | Adds sign-up, login, and per-user data separation — meaningfully larger scope. |
| **Custom** | Something else | Tell me the shape you have in mind. |

---

**Please review the spec.** You can read the full file at `specs/001-bookmark-manager/spec.md`. Let me know:

1. Your answer to **Q1**, and
2. Whether the stories, scope, and out-of-scope items look right — anything to add, cut, or change.

Once you approve the spec (with any edits), I'll move to the **plan** gate with `speckit-plan`. I won't plan or write any code until then.

Option A: single user with no login.

The draft is a good start, but it leaves out several things I consider part of managing bookmarks, so I’m not ready to approve it yet.

When I save a link, I want the app to collect the page’s title, description, icon, and preview image automatically, while still letting me edit the title and description. If the address already exists, it should take me to the existing bookmark for editing instead of merely warning me.

Please also include:

- Notes on bookmarks, with simple formatting and note text included in search.
- Existing-tag suggestions while adding tags.
- Case-insensitive search across titles, descriptions, notes, and addresses, including `#tag`, exact phrases, and combinations such as AND, OR, NOT, and parentheses.
- Read-later status, with a separate unread view and the ability to mark items read.
- Archiving as a reversible action, separate from permanent deletion, with archived items hidden from normal lists and searches.
- Selecting multiple bookmarks—and optionally everything matching the current view—to tag, mark read or unread, archive, or delete.
- Sorting by useful choices such as date added and title.
- Saved searches that can combine text with included and excluded tags.
- A readable list showing the title, description, tags, and site icon.
- A saved local copy of the page, storing the PDF itself when the link is a PDF, plus an option to preserve it through the Internet Archive.
- Import and export using the common browser-bookmark HTML format.
- Basic display preferences such as default sorting, number of items shown, and text size.

Tags feel central rather than an optional final layer, so I would move them earlier. Automatic page information, import/export, and saved copies should not be listed as out of scope. Browser extensions, cross-device syncing, accounts, and sign-in can remain out of scope for this version.

## 📄 Revised specification ready for review

`specs/001-bookmark-manager/spec.md` — all quality-checklist items now pass.

### What changed from your feedback

- **Q1 resolved**: single user, no login — baked into Assumptions.
- **Saving is now richer (US1)**: automatic capture of title, description, site icon, and preview image; title/description stay editable; a page that can't be fetched still saves with graceful fallback. **Duplicate address now opens the existing bookmark for editing** instead of just warning.
- **Tags promoted to a core story (US3, P2)**, with existing-tag **suggestions** while typing.
- **Notes (US4)** with simple formatting, included in search.
- **Powerful search (US5)**: case-insensitive across titles, descriptions, notes, addresses; `#tag` terms; `"exact phrases"`; and `AND` / `OR` / `NOT` / parentheses.
- **Read-later (US6)** with a separate unread view.
- **Archiving (US7)** as a reversible action, hidden from normal lists/searches — distinct from permanent delete.
- **Bulk actions (US8)**: select many, or everything matching the current view, to tag / mark read-unread / archive / delete.
- **Saved searches (US9)** combining text with included **and** excluded tags.
- **Sorting + display preferences (US10)**: date added, title; default sort, item count, text size.
- **Saved local copies (US11)**: page snapshot, the PDF itself for PDF links, plus optional Internet Archive preservation.
- **Import/export (US12)** in the standard browser-bookmark HTML format.
- **Readable list** shows title, description, tags, and site icon.
- **Scope updated**: automatic page info, import/export, and saved copies are now **in scope**; browser extensions, cross-device sync, and accounts/sign-in remain **out of scope**.

### Two honesty notes flagged as dependencies (not blockers)

- **Automatic page info & saved copies need to fetch the live page** — when a page is unreachable, the app degrades gracefully rather than failing the save.
- **Internet Archive preservation depends on that external third-party service** — if it's down, your local copy and bookmark are unaffected and the failure is reported honestly.

I read *"simple formatting"* on notes as lightweight styling (bold, italics, lists, links), not a full document editor — noted in Assumptions. Say the word if you meant something heavier.

---

**Please review.** Anything to add, cut, or re-prioritize? Once you approve the spec, I'll move to the **plan** gate (`speckit-plan`) and present the implementation plan before any code is written.

This is very close, and lightweight Markdown for notes—bold, italics, lists, and links—is exactly what I meant.

Please make four small corrections before I approve it:

- Bulk tag actions should support both adding and removing tags.
- Import and export should preserve each bookmark’s title, tags, and original date added, not just its address.
- A saved web-page copy should be a self-contained local HTML file; PDF links should still store the PDF itself.
- Search should make clear that ordinary text combined with `#tag` narrows results using both conditions. Also, quoted words such as `"AND"` should be treated as literal search text rather than as search instructions.

Everything else, including the priorities and out-of-scope items, looks right. Once those points are included, I’m happy for this to move to planning.

## 📐 Implementation plan ready for review

**Feature**: `001-bookmark-manager` · **Constitution check**: PASS (the constitution is an unratified template, so there are no gates to violate; the plan still follows the CLAUDE.md SDD conventions).

**Artifacts generated:**
- `plan.md` — the plan (summary, tech context, structure)
- `research.md` — 10 technical decisions with rationale and rejected alternatives
- `data-model.md` — 5 entities (Bookmark, Tag, SavedCopy, SavedSearch, Preferences) mapped to FRs
- `contracts/api.md` — the JSON API surface
- `contracts/search-query.md` — the search grammar (incl. your `#tag`-narrows and literal-`"AND"` rules)
- `contracts/bookmark-html.md` — the import/export format (preserving title, tags, date added)
- `quickstart.md` — how to run + a validation scenario per user story

### The approach in plain terms

A **single small web app** — one Node.js server that both serves the page and stores your data locally. No accounts, no cloud database, no external services except the optional Internet Archive.

| Concern | Choice | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Where data lives | A local **SQLite** file + saved-copy files under `data/` | Durable, no external database, survives restarts |
| Page info & snapshots | Server fetches the page; **Chromium** (already installed) makes the self-contained HTML copy; PDFs stored as files | Matches your saved-copy corrections; degrades gracefully if a page is unreachable |
| Search | A **purpose-built query engine** | Needed to honor your exact rules: text + `#tag` narrows by both, and quoted `"AND"` is literal |
| Notes | Markdown (bold/italics/lists/links), sanitized | Exactly the lightweight formatting you confirmed |
| The screen | A **framework-free** single-page app | Keeps it simple; fast to load |
| Internet Archive | Isolated service, failure reported honestly | Your bookmark is never lost if the service is down |

### How the work is sliced

Ordered by your priorities, so each slice is demonstrable on its own:
- **MVP first**: US1 (save with auto info) + US2 (browse & open)
- **Then P2**: tags, notes/edit/delete, powerful search, read-later, archive
- **Then P3**: bulk actions, saved searches, sorting/preferences, saved copies, import/export

### Two honesty notes carried from the spec
- Auto page-info and snapshots require fetching the live page — unreachable pages still save (just with less detail).
- Internet Archive is a third party — if it's down, preservation fails cleanly and your data is untouched. In the review environment, outbound internet access to fetch arbitrary pages / reach the Archive may be limited; where it is, I'll use local fixtures for tests and report honestly rather than fake success.

---

**Please review the plan** (`specs/001-bookmark-manager/plan.md` and the artifacts above). Does the technology approach, data model, and slicing look right to you? Any concerns about SQLite, the vanilla-JS UI, or anything else?

Once you approve the plan, I'll run **`speckit-tasks`** to generate the actionable task breakdown (and present that too) before any implementation begins.

The plan looks right to me. I’m comfortable with the local SQLite storage and the simple browser interface, and the planned handling of page information, saved copies, search, and service failures matches what we agreed.

## ✅ MVP implemented and verified — paused for your review

**Tasks T001–T020 complete** (Setup → Foundational → US1 Save + US2 Browse/Open), marked `[X]` in `tasks.md`.

### How to review it
The app is registered with the runtime (`/work/.harness/app.json`, port 4000). Open **http://maker:4000**. The broker starts it automatically. You'll land on an **empty state** ("No bookmarks yet") — from there:
- Click **+ Add bookmark**, paste any address (scheme optional, e.g. `example.com`), Save.
- The title/description/icon/preview are **fetched automatically**; you can edit the title & description and they persist.
- Saving an address you already have **opens the existing bookmark** instead of duplicating.
- The **All** list shows each bookmark with title, description, host, and icon; the title opens in a new tab.

> Note on the review environment: automatic page-info needs to fetch the live page. If this container's outbound internet is restricted, a save still succeeds — it just falls back to a title derived from the address (by design). Everything else works fully offline.

### Verification (actually run, all green)
- **Unit:** 3/3 pass (metadata parsing + fallback).
- **Browser e2e (Playwright 1.61.0, shared Chromium):** 7/7 pass — auto-capture, edit-persists-after-reload, duplicate→existing, unreachable→derived title, invalid→error, empty state, list fields, open-in-new-tab.

### One implementation adaptation (transparent)
I swapped the SQLite **driver** from `better-sqlite3` to Node 24's **built-in `node:sqlite`**. The prebuilt `better-sqlite3` binary core-dumps at process teardown under Node 24 — a bad trait for a server the harness stops/starts. The built-in module is API-compatible, needs no native build, and shuts down cleanly. This is a driver detail; the plan's "file-based SQLite" architecture is unchanged. I updated `plan.md`, `research.md` (§D2), and the task note to reflect it.

### What's next (awaiting your go-ahead)
Per your instruction, I'm **pausing here**. When you're ready, I'll continue with the P2 stories in order — **US3 Tags → US4 Notes/edit/delete → US5 Search → US6 Read-later → US7 Archive** — then the P3 stories (bulk, saved searches, sorting/preferences, saved copies, import/export), validating each as I go.

The complete application is built, tested, and ready for your final review.

## ✅ Bookmark Manager — complete and verified

All **67 tasks** across all 12 user stories are implemented and marked done. The app is registered with the runtime (`.harness/app.json`, port 4000) — open **http://maker:4000**. The broker starts it automatically, serving a small set of sample bookmarks so you can see every feature immediately (4 active, 1 archived, with tags and notes).

### Verification (all actually run, all green)

| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| **Unit tests** (`npm test`) | **18/18 pass** — search parser (every contract example), Markdown sanitization, metadata parsing, import/export round-trip |
| **Browser e2e** (Playwright 1.61.0, shared Chromium) | **30/30 pass** — one per user story + the two you added + cross-cutting |
| **Performance** (`tests/perf/seed.js`) | Search over **1,000 bookmarks in ~1ms**; bulk over 60 in ~2ms (SC-005/SC-006) |
| **Cross-cutting** | Data survives server restart (SC-004); archive→restore preserves tags/notes/copies (SC-007) |

### What's delivered, by story
- **US1** Save with auto title/description/icon/preview; duplicate → opens existing; graceful fallback when a page is unreachable
- **US2** Readable list (title, description, tags, icon); open in new tab; empty state
- **US3** Tags with existing-tag suggestions; filter by tag
- **US4** Markdown notes (bold/italics/lists/links, sanitized); edit all fields; delete with confirmation — *plus your added browser check*
- **US5** Case-insensitive search across title/description/note/address; `#tag` (narrows with text); `"phrases"`; `AND/OR/NOT`/parentheses; quoted `"AND"` literal — *plus your added note-through-search check*
- **US6** Read-later status + unread view · **US7** Reversible archiving, hidden from lists/search
- **US8** Bulk add/remove tag, read/unread, archive, delete — on a selection or everything matching the view
- **US9** Saved searches (text + included/excluded tags) · **US10** Sorting + persisted display prefs (sort, page size, text size)
- **US11** Saved copies: self-contained HTML for pages, the PDF itself for PDFs, optional Internet Archive with honest failure
- **US12** Import/export in Netscape bookmark HTML, preserving title/tags/original date, skipping duplicates — *plus your added browser check*

### Two honest implementation notes (recorded in the artifacts)
- **Storage driver**: `node:sqlite` instead of `better-sqlite3` (Node 24 teardown crash) — same file-based SQLite architecture.
- **Snapshots**: self-contained HTML is produced by fetch + resource-inlining rather than headless Chromium — same offline-openable result, lighter and deterministic. Both are documented in `research.md`.

Every network-dependent feature degrades gracefully, and in this review environment (where outbound internet to arbitrary sites / the Internet Archive may be restricted) the app falls back honestly rather than faking success — the e2e suite proves the behavior with local fixtures.

The spec, plan, tasks, and design docs in `specs/001-bookmark-manager/` are all current. Please take a look at http://maker:4000 — happy to adjust anything through the spec if you'd like changes.

The completed application matches the behavior we approved, and the verification covers all twelve stories, including the additional note-search and import/export checks. The storage and snapshot adaptations preserve the outcomes I asked for.
